title: HB316 (2024 Regular): Crimes and Corrections - Penalties and Procedures (Violent Firearms Offender Act of 2024)

other_topics: judicial-criminal-justice: Section 2 (Correctional Services § 9-609.2) — reentry kit and Medicaid help for people leaving state prison

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2024RS/bills/hb/hb0316f.pdf)
provenance.note: First reader (as filed, January 15, 2024); no enrolled text was read. Section 1 only renumbers Public Safety § 5-134(c) and (d). Section 2 also adds Correctional Services § 9-609.2 (reentry kit), not quoted because it is not a gun part. In § 4-306(b) and § 5-133(b) the bracketed old numbering and words were left out of the quotes. No passage vote is recorded.

operative_text:
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Correctional Services § 6-101(m)): “Technical violation” means a violation of a condition of probation, parole, or mandatory supervision that does not involve: ... (4) absconding; OR (5) USE OR POSSESSION OF A FIREARM.
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4-204): “USE A FIREARM” DOES NOT INCLUDE THE MERE POSSESSION OF A FIREARM. ... A person who violates this section is guilty of a FELONY and, in addition to any other penalty imposed for the crime of violence or felony, shall be sentenced to imprisonment for not less than 5 years and not exceeding 20 years.
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4-306(b)): A person who uses an assault weapon, a rapid fire trigger activator, or a magazine that has a capacity of more than 10 rounds of ammunition, in the commission of a felony or a crime of violence as defined in § 5–101 of the Public Safety Article is guilty of a FELONY and on conviction, in addition to any other sentence imposed for the felony or crime of violence, shall be sentenced under this subsection.
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 4-404): A person may not use or possess a machine gun in the commission or attempted commission of a FELONY OR crime of violence.
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Criminal Law § 14-101(a)): use of a firearm in the commission of a felony or other crime of violence;
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-133(b)(2)): EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN SUBSECTION (C) OF THIS SECTION, A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A MISDEMEANOR AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO: 1. EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN ITEM 2 OF THIS SUBPARAGRAPH, IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 5 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH; AND 2. SUBJECT TO PARAGRAPH (3) OF THIS SUBSECTION, FOR A SECOND OR SUBSEQUENT OFFENSE, IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS OR A FINE NOT EXCEEDING $10,000 OR BOTH.
Section 2 (Md. Code Ann., Public Safety § 5-134(c)): A DEALER OR OTHER PERSON MAY NOT SELL, RENT, LOAN, OR TRANSFER A REGULATED FIREARM TO A PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE IF THE DEALER OR OTHER PERSON HAS ACTUAL KNOWLEDGE THAT THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, BORROWER, OR TRANSFEREE INTENDS TO USE THE REGULATED FIREARM TO: (I) COMMIT A CRIME; OR (II) CAUSE HARM TO THE PURCHASER, LESSEE, TRANSFEREE, OR RECIPIENT OR ANOTHER PERSON. ... A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SUBSECTION IS GUILTY OF A FELONY AND ON CONVICTION IS SUBJECT TO IMPRISONMENT NOT EXCEEDING 10 YEARS.
